title: The Perfect 5-Minute Exercise Break For Students And Teachers dents-and-teachers/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin shares a five-move, five-minute workout designed to relieve boredom and reverse the physical effects of prolonged sitting, using one minute each of continuous movement per exercise with no rest between sets. The moves — Twist, Wring, Shove, Circle, and Ski — progressively raise heart rate while engaging different muscle groups, from a gentle warm-up rotation to a more demanding standing ab and full-body sequence. He emphasizes that proper technique matters as much as the exercise itself, since focused movement is meditative, reinforces precise classroom habits, and prevents students from cutting corners. The routine is pitched as usable across ages from kindergarten to high school PE, with an option to repeat the sequence twice for a longer, more complete break.

quotes: A short exercise break can relieve boredom, improve thinking , and reverse the negative health effects of sitting.
It must be targeted in a way that increases your heart rate yet stimulates every muscle in the body.
The Twist is a great exercise to begin with because it feels good after long sitting. It slowly warms the body and prepares it for the next, more challenging exercise.
The wring is a standing ab exercise that works the lower, middle, and upper sections of the abdominal wall while also increasing your heart rate.
First, focused movement is meditative and will clear their mind of unwanted stress and tension. Second, it conditions your students to do everything in your classroom in a certain, very specific way.
I’ve used the same rotation of exercises as a warm-up for high school PE, but they’re also simple and gentle enough for kindergarten or even pre-K students.
